gates.name: Python library decode keeps pace with the Rust library
gates.why: write_csv(order_rows(reader)) should be the Rust chain with a thin Python entry; a stage reading the stream through Python instead once cost 17%.

gates.name: Python CLI keeps pace with the Rust library
gates.why: aero1553.cli.main runs the Rust CLI in-process; only the call into it is Python.

gates.name: Python merge keeps pace with the Rust merge
gates.why: merge_readers hands the Rust merge its readers; the merged stream never leaves Rust.

gates.name: Python record iteration stays cheap
gates.why: Iterating in Python builds one record object per record, lazily: it should cost a small multiple of the Rust read, not an order of magnitude.

gates.name: columns() stays far ahead of per-record dicts
gates.why: The point of columns(): a table with no Python object per record. If building one from to_dict() dicts gets close, columns() has regressed.

gates.name: numeric columns cost a small multiple of a bare Rust read
gates.why: Without the text fields, columns() builds no per-record Python object, so a DataFrame of them should cost little over reading the file.
